verses.zh: 亚撒的儿子约沙法接续他作王，奋勇自强，防备以色列人，
verses.en: His son Jehoshaphat replaced him as king and solidified his rule over Israel.[NOTE:1]
verses.commentary:
17:1 "Jehoshaphat" "Jehoshaphat" means "YHWH is Judge" (BDB 221). 2 Chronicles 17-20 deals with his reign.
This material is not in Kings and, therefore, comes from the Chronicler's prophet source or other written annals (cf. 2 Chr. 16:11).

There may have been a three year co-reign with Asa (because of Asa's debilitating foot disease). Therefore,
the "third year" of 2 Chr. 17:17 would have been his first year after the death of Asa.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF THE DIVIDED KINGDOM

NASB, JB
"over Israel"

NKJV, NRSV, TEV, NJB, REB, LXX, Peshitta
"against Israel"

JPSOA
"took a firm hold of Israel"

Again Judah is called "Israel" (NASB, JB, JPSOA). The implication is that Judah is the true descendant
of Jacob.

The MT has the preposition על, which has a large semantic

range (BDB 752-759). 2 Chronicles 17:2 seems to support "against." The powerful northern King, Ahab, mentioned so
predominately in Kings, is the focus.

verses.zh: 安置军兵在犹大一切坚固城里，又安置防兵在犹大地和他父亚撒所得以法莲的城邑中。
verses.en: He placed troops in all Judah’s fortified cities and posted garrisons[NOTE:1] throughout the land of Judah and in the cities of Ephraim that his father Asa had seized.
verses.commentary:
17:2 "in the cities of Ephraim which Asa his father had captured" This goes back to 2 Chr. 13:19; 15:8. It would
include "Ramah" (2 Chr. 16:1).

verses.zh: 耶和华与约沙法同在；因为他行他祖大卫初行的道，不寻求巴力，
verses.en: The Lord was with Jehoshaphat because he followed in his ancestor[NOTE:1] David’s footsteps at the beginning of his reign.[NOTE:2] He did not seek the Baals,
notes: Heb “for he walked in the ways of David his father [in] the beginning [times].”
verses.commentary:
17:3-9 "The Lord was with Jehoshaphat" There are several reasons given.

- He followed the example of early David, 2 Chr. 17:3 (i.e., the Davidic covenant of 2 Samuel 7; 1 Chronicles 17 is the
theological key, cf. 2 Kgs. 2:2; 2 Chr. 34:2).

- He did not practice fertility worship, 2 Chr. 17:3.

- He sought the God of David, 2 Chr. 17:4 (see note at 2 Chr. 7:14).

- He obeyed YHWH's commandments, 2 Chr. 17:4 (see Special Topic: Keep).

- He did not act like the northern tribes, 2 Chr. 17:4.

- He took pride in the ways of the Lord, 2 Chr. 17:6 (lit. "his heart was high in the ways of YHWH").

- He removed the high places, 2 Chr. 17:6.

- He sent

- five officials

- nine Levites (cf. 2 chr. 35:3)

- two priests

into the cities of Judah to teach the Law of Moses, 2 Chr. 17:7-9 (cf. Deut. 6:4-9; 33:10).

The Chronicler does not spend any space or ink on Ahab and Jezebel!

17:3 "his father David" The MT is supported by the Peshitta, but some MSS of the LXX have "his father,"
implying Asa. Asa also was faithful only during his early years.

"earlier days" There is some confusion in the Hebrew text. This could refer to

- Asa (LXX)

- David (MT, Peshitta)

- Jehoshaphat (NIV, see Expositor's Bible Commentary, vol. 4, p. 496)

"the Baals" Ba'al was the male fertility god of the Canaanite pantheon. This worship could be expressed
as a singular (cf. 1 Kgs. 16:31) or a plural, as here (cf. 1 Kgs. 18:18). This fertility god was worshiped by imitation magic
at local high places (i.e., ritual sex). Every town and village had their own high place.

17:3,6 "Baal. . .Asherim" These were the male and female gods of Canaanite fertility worship.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP OF THE ANE

verses.zh: 只寻求他父亲的　神，遵行他的诫命，不效法以色列人的行为。
verses.en: but instead sought the God of his ancestors[NOTE:1] and obeyed[NOTE:2] his commands, unlike the Israelites.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and not like the behavior of Israel.”

verses.zh: 所以耶和华坚定他的国，犹大众人给他进贡；约沙法大有尊荣资财。
verses.en: The Lord made his kingdom secure;[NOTE:1] all Judah brought tribute to Jehoshaphat, and he became very wealthy and greatly respected.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “established the kingdom in his hand.”
Heb “and he had wealth and honor in abundance.”
verses.commentary:
17:5 YHWH blessed Jehoshaphat by

- establishing his kingdom, 2 Chr. 17:5

- all Judah bringing tribute, 2 Chr. 17:5

- expected gifts to a new king

- taxes, cf. 1 Sam. 10:27; 1 Kgs. 10:25

- great riches and honor, 2 Chr. 17:5

- protection from attack by the surrounding nations because of their dread of YHWH, 2 Chr. 17:10

- gifts brought by Philistines, 2 Chr. 17:11

- animals brought by Arabians, 2 Chr. 17:11 (Josephus, Antiq. 8.15.1., says they brought more every year)

- he grew greater and greater, 2 Chr. 17:12

- built cities

- large army

verses.zh: 他高兴遵行耶和华的道，并且从犹大除掉一切邱坛和木偶。
verses.en: He was committed to following the Lord;[NOTE:1] he even removed the high places and Asherah poles from Judah.
notes: Heb “and his heart was high in the ways of the Lord.” Perhaps גָּבַהּ (gavah, “be high”) here means “be cheerful” (HALOT 171 s.v.) or “be encouraged” (BDB 147 s.v. 3.a).
verses.commentary:
17:6 "He took great pride in the ways of the Lord" This is literally "his heart was lifted up,"
which usually denotes a prideful event (cf. Deut. 8:14; 2 Chr. 26:16; Ps. 131:1), but here it is a positive attitude toward YHWH and
His Law.

"and again removed the high places" Asa also tried to remove the local Ba'al and Asherah worship sites
but the people kept reopening them (cf. 2 Chr. 15:17; 20:33). They are removed again under Hezekiah (cf. 2 Kgs. 18:4) and
Josiah (cf. 2 Kgs. 23:4-8).

verses.zh: 他作王第三年，就差遣臣子便亥伊勒、俄巴底、撒迦利雅、拿坦业、米该亚往犹大各城去教训百姓。
verses.en: In the third year of his reign he sent his officials Ben Hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah to teach in the cities of Judah.
verses.commentary:
17:7

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, TEV, NJB, JPSOA
"Ben-hail"

LXX
"the sons of the mighty"

Peshitta
"the commanders of the armies"

AB
"outstanding men"

The name "Ben-hail" (BDB 122) occurs only here. Why the ancient versions took it as a descriptive phrase
and not a name is uncertain. Possibly, "ben," "son of. . .," caused the confusion. These government or royal leaders did not do
the teaching but acted as governmental enforcers or organizers.

verses.zh: 同着他们有利未人示玛雅、尼探雅、西巴第雅、亚撒黑、示米拉末、约拿单、亚多尼雅、多比雅、驼巴多尼雅，又有祭司以利沙玛、约兰同着他们。
verses.en: They were accompanied by the Levites Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tob-Adonijah, and by the priests Elishama and Jehoram.

verses.zh: 他们带着耶和华的律法书，走遍犹大各城教训百姓。
verses.en: They taught throughout Judah, taking with them the scroll of the law of the Lord. They traveled to all the cities of Judah and taught the people.
verses.commentary:
17:9 "the book of the law of the Lord" One wonders what this book contained
(cf. Deut. 17:18-20; 2 Chr. 34:14; Neh. 9:3).

- all the Pentateuch

- Deuteronomy only

- some of the historical books

The verse implies that Jehoshaphat had many copies of the Law made so that each group could have a
copy to teach the people from.

verses.zh: 耶和华使犹大四围的列国都甚恐惧，不敢与约沙法争战。
verses.en: The Lord put fear into all the kingdoms surrounding Judah;[NOTE:1] they did not make war with Jehoshaphat.
notes: Heb “and the terror of the Lord was upon all the kingdoms of the lands which were surrounding Judah.”
verses.commentary:
17:10 "the dread of the Lord" There are many Hebrew terms that express this concept.
Fear can be a good thing (i.e., Jer. 32:40) when it is used in the sense of awe or reverence , but in this context, it refers to the
divine fear of YHWH given to the covenant people's enemies (cf. Exod. 15:14-16; 23:27; Deut. 2:25; 11:25; Ps. 105:38;
2 Chr. 14:14).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR

verses.zh: 有些非利士人与约沙法送礼物，纳贡银。阿拉伯人也送他公绵羊七千七百只，公山羊七千七百只。
verses.en: Some of the Philistines brought Jehoshaphat tribute, including a load of silver. The Arabs brought him 7,700 rams and 7,700 goats from their flocks.

verses.zh: 约沙法日渐强大，在犹大建造营寨和积货城。
verses.en: Jehoshaphat’s power kept increasing. He built fortresses and storage cities throughout Judah.

verses.zh: 他在犹大城邑中有许多工程，又在耶路撒冷有战士，就是大能的勇士。
verses.en: He had many supplies stored in the cities of Judah and an army of skilled warriors stationed in Jerusalem.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and many supplies were his in the cities of Judah, and men of war, warriors of skill in Jerusalem.”map For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

verses.zh: 他们的数目，按着宗族，记在下面：犹大族的千夫长押拿为首率领大能的勇士―三十万；
verses.en: These were their divisions by families: There were 1,000 officers from Judah.[NOTE:1] Adnah the commander led 300,000 skilled warriors,
notes: Or perhaps “from Judah, commanders of the thousands.”
verses.commentary:
17:14-18 These numbers add up to over a million. They probably represent military units of a much smaller number.

- the NASB Study Bible, p. 606, suggests "300 units. . .280 units. . .200 units. . .200 units. . .180 units"

- the Expositor's Bible Commentary, vol. 4, p. 497, suggests that "'eleph" (thousand) should be "'allup" (leader)

- אלף ‒ thousand

- אלוף ‒ chief

- however, NIDOTTE, vol. 1, p. 407, rejects this identification
There is obviously some form of conscription for labor and the military in 2 Chronicles.

- Asa ‒ 2 Chr. 14:7 (for labor)

- Jehoshaphat ‒ here, (for military)

- Amaziah ‒ 2 Chr. 25:5 (for military)

- Uzziah ‒ 2 Chr. 26:11-13 (for military)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THOUSAND (eleph)

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- How does 2 Chr. 17:1-2 refer to Ahab, King of Israel, without mentioning him?

- To what does the adjective "earlier" refer?

- List the ways Jehoshaphat followed YHWH.

- What were "the high places"?

- Why is 2 Chr. 17:7 unique?

- What does "the book of the law of the Lord" include?

- Explain "the dread of the Lord."

- Why can the numbers of 2 Chr. 17:14-18 not be taken literally?

verses.zh: 其次是，千夫长约哈难率领大能的勇士―二十八万；
其次是，细基利的儿子亚玛斯雅〈他为耶和华牺牲自己〉率领大能的勇士―二十万。
verses.en: and Amasiah son of Zikri, who volunteered to serve the Lord, led 200,000 skilled warriors.

verses.zh: 便雅悯族，是大能的勇士以利雅大率领拿弓箭和盾牌的―二十万；
verses.en: From Benjamin, Eliada, a skilled warrior, led 200,000 men who were equipped with bows and shields,

verses.zh: 其次是，约萨拔率领预备打仗的―十八万。
这都是伺候王的，还有王在犹大全地坚固城所安置的不在其内。
verses.en: These were the ones who served the king, besides those whom the king placed in the fortified cities throughout Judah.
